instrument: Watchdog, kennel main 6a05dfb6c, rubric-2026.10.1; contained scans (codehealth-analyzer:train-src-89d1e8def87553cc)

inputs.catalog: rubric-2026.10.1: 165 dimensions, lenses identical to coverage/matrix.json

definitions.dimension: sum over repositories of the harness's per-dimension rows (matching re-run within the dimension); a plant counts under every dimension its concept maps to, so rows overlap
definitions.lens: plants/traps once per lens from the per-concept rows (found = TP of the whole run); results and noise = sum of the lens's dimension rows (every result has one dimension)
definitions.noiseKinds: trap-fp = on a must-not-fire trap; clean-fp = in a certified-clean region; na-fp = a concept the key declares not applicable; unmatched-fp = a covered concept's result matching no entry
definitions.fnMissedByRun: dimension-level FNs that no dimension found (global FN); the rest were found by another dimension (fnFoundByOtherDimension)

noiseBacklog.mechanism: AC4 'Click handler on a non-interactive <dialog>' fires on the native modal <dialog> element's backdrop-dismiss handler; the dismiss-backdrop escape (EventHandlers.IsDismissBackdrop) recognises a wrapper of a role="dialog"/aria-modal descendant, not the native modal element itself.

AC4 'Click handler on a non-interactive <article>' fires when an inner native <button> performs the same action through a different handler function; the duplicated-action escape compares handler identity, not the action performed.

AC6 'Low contrast colour pair in CSS (3.8:1) ... below the 4.5:1 WCAG AA minimum for normal text' does not read font-size/font-weight declared in the same rule, so large text (3:1 bar) is judged against the normal-text bar.

AX1 'Captive dependency: singleton X captures transient Y' fires even when the transient implementation has no fields and is not IDisposable, so one captured instance behaves exactly like a fresh one per call.

AXB1.name: Runtime evidence locked — no reproducible boot

noiseBacklog.mechanism: C1 'No data-protection/encryption ... sensitive data at rest may be unprotected. If TDE/KMS/vault is delegated to infrastructure, ignore.' fires on every service lacking encryption APIs in code, without evidence that sensitive data is stored or that storage is self-managed — the row tells the reader to ignore it in exactly the common case.

C2 reports 'No named authorization policies ... who may do what is encoded inline' on TypeScript/Express services whose scopes are named constants and whose every route declares its required scope at registration (requireScope(Scopes.x)) — the TS equivalent of a named policy is not recognised.

C2 'Thin authorization enforcement: Only N place(s) refuse an unauthorized caller — too few to demonstrate default-deny' counts textual refusal sites, so centralising the check in one verifier lowers the evidence.

C3 'Partial audit-trail evidence ... missing: an EF SaveChanges interceptor ... [Audited] per-entity coverage' asks for EF write-side hooks in a file-backed service that has no database and no entity write path.
C3 scores audit-trail evidence at 90 because an event-sourced stream exists, without checking that the stream covers the sensitive data or records the actor.

D1/D2 report a route-registration factory over threshold although the message itself says most points belong to function literals declared inside it ('4 of the 20 points are its own statements'); D15 then builds a hotspot from that complexity plus two same-day authoring commits.
D1 'cyclomatic 17 (threshold 15)' fires on a method that is one flat disjunction of eight independent range tests with no nesting.

D5 'Off the main sequence' publishes a finding for every concrete, stable library (domain core, application layer, contracts) with distance >= 0.7, including rows whose own text says 'the shape a shared-kernel / building-block library has BY DESIGN' — a row that concedes the shape is healthy is still emitted.

The TS coverage run installs with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, which skips native-binding install steps (libxmljs2's prebuilt binding); every suite that imports the application then fails to load, and D8 publishes per-file 'Low coverage: 0.0%' rows for the whole route layer as a fact about the repository instead of degrading the measurement.

D8 ('Low coverage: 0.0%') and R4 ('No test reaches this file') report composition roots, process entry points, release scripts and thin browser glue over vendor SDKs as untested; the reachability/coverage fact is right, but the implied 'must be unit-tested' does not apply to wiring files whose collaborators are each tested.

D8 'Low coverage: X: 33.3% line coverage (3/9)' is emitted for exception types whose only uncovered lines are the standard constructors CA1032 requires; the percentage is accurate but the rows carry no behavioural risk.
D8 emits 'Coverage not measured — no coverage collector is wired up' as a result row although it is an engine abstention ('excluded from score by design'), not a claim about the code.

D10 'No assertions ... no assertion call was recognised' does not know CsCheck's Sample(predicate) (and similar property-based APIs), which throw CsCheckException with the shrunk counter-example when the predicate is false.

D13's name-driven 'signing-key' rule accepts a GUID-shaped value under a property whose NAME contains Secret/SigningKey (SecretRotationJobId, stripeKeySecretId, webhookSigningKeyId) and reports it as a leaked key; and because D13 de-duplicates per (secret type, file), such a row can swallow a real key elsewhere in the same file.
D14 matches banned SPDX ids as SUBSTRINGS of the resolved id (to catch -only/-or-later), so the banned 'GPL-2.0' matches 'LGPL-2.0-only' and an LGPL package is reported as GPL-banned.
D16 emits a repository-level 'Further sole-owners (lower concentration)' row for files below the off-boarding threshold without naming them, so the row cannot be acted on or adjudicated per file.

D17 'AnalyzerSeverityNone' reports a `dotnet_diagnostic.<id>.severity = none` line in .editorconfig as an undocumented, repository-wide suppression ('the only record that it was ever switched off is this line') even when the comment on the line directly above states the reason and a nested src/.editorconfig re-enables the rule for all production code.

D17 'WriteOnlyPrivateField' reports a private System.Threading.Timer field that is assigned once and never read, although the field reference is what keeps the timer from being garbage-collected (and so keeps it firing).

D17 dead-code (SymbolFinder walk) reports an IDesignTimeDbContextFactory<T> implementation as unreferenced; dotnet-ef discovers and instantiates it by reflection, which the walk cannot see and no reflection-entry-point allow-list covers.

D18 'Thin analysable surface across projects ... Consolidate thin projects' counts host/composition-root projects and shared ServiceDefaults libraries as thin projects to merge, although they are thin by design.

D19's model-judged README pass reports 'no licence statement' / 'no contributor guidance' for READMEs that contain a '## License' / '## Contributing' section; wording varies run to run, the claim does not.
D20 model-judged ADR review flags 'The Consequences section is incomplete' when an ADR records its consequences but not the model's preferred list of benefits and trade-offs.

D21 (model-judged naming consistency) emits rows whose text concludes 'These are distinct operations ... No inconsistency.: No change needed.' — the model's negative verdicts are published as findings.
D21 model-judged naming reports two different concepts with a shared stem (a decision code `NoShow` and a fee amount `NoShowFee`) as one concept named inconsistently.

D23 'Cross-context type X (A -> B) ... exposed in B's public surface ... couples the contexts' derives a type's bounded context from its PROJECT/assembly, so a context's own Domain types used by its own Application layer, integration events from the published Contracts project, and the shared messaging kernel are all reported as cross-context coupling.

D24 model-judged 'redundant comment' asks to remove grouping headings inside long registration methods ('// Persistence', '// E-mail and reminders') and comments stating a physical purpose the code cannot express.

D26 'Projects may be oversized for their cohesion: 1 of 1 project(s) ... (repository root) 3011 LoC, 151 module-visible types across 18 directories' treats a single small TS service package as an oversized project to split.

Semgrep 'res-render-injection' reports a service method that happens to be named `render` (ImageMagick thumbnail renderer, a Nunjucks card renderer with a fixed template name, a report layout) as Express `res.render` with request-controlled template selection.
The watchdog-authored D29 rule for DTD-enabled XmlDocument loading matches `SignedXml.LoadXml(XmlElement)` — a method on SignedXml that takes an already-parsed element and parses no text.

Semgrep 'unsafe-path-combine' reports Path.Combine(sourceDirectory, name) where the directory is the operator's own CLI argument (the trust boundary of an admin tool) and the name was validated against [A-Z0-9-]{1,32} before use.
Semgrep 'xpath-injection' (security-audit) reports an XPath built from a value that was passed through XmlConvert.VerifyNCName, which the rule does not model as a sanitiser.

watchdog-assembled-code-string-evaluated-ts reports `new Function` over source assembled only from a fixed table keyed by a schema-validated enum and a literal '1'/'-1' sign — no request text reaches the string.

watchdog-open-redirect-default-operand-js fires on `res.redirect(sameSitePath(req.query.returnTo) ?? '/')`: the left operand is a same-site-path validator's return value, but the rule treats any expression containing req.query as the raw request value.

D31 republishes trivy DS-0026 'No HEALTHCHECK defined' and augments it with 'Without one the runtime only knows whether the process is alive ... so a wedged container is restarted by nobody', on images whose only runtime is Kubernetes — which ignores Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK and uses the Deployment's liveness/readiness probes.

D31 republishes checkov CKV_K8S_35 'Prefer using secrets as files over secrets as environment variables' as a Medium IaC defect on Deployments that inject secrets with env.valueFrom.secretKeyRef — a hardening preference, not a defect — and anchors the row at the resource's first line rather than the secretKeyRef line.

D31 republishes trivy KSV-0125 'Restrict container images to trusted registries ... uses an image from an untrusted registry' for every image, with no notion of which registry the owner trusts; a registry allow-list is a cluster admission-policy control, not a workload-manifest defect.

D31 republishes checkov CKV_K8S_40 / KSV-0020 'Containers should run as a high UID to avoid host conflict' on a pod that already runs non-root with every other hardening control; a UID range is a preference, not a privilege boundary. Reported at deployment.yaml:1 and the container line instead of the runAsUser line.
D31 republishes checkov CKV_K8S_38 'Ensure that Service Account Tokens are only mounted where necessary' on a DaemonSet whose configuration queries the API server, i.e. where the token is necessary.

watchdog-personal-data-in-url (D32) and S1 'Request payload sent in the URL query string ... interpolated `email` query parameter' key on the parameter name `email`; the value is a boolean channel flag and the subject is addressed by an opaque id.

D39 'IL efficiency: N authored method(s) exceed the IL budget (> 250 instructions)' reports start-up-only methods — DI registration extensions and EF IEntityTypeConfiguration.Configure — whose IL size has no runtime cost consequence.

D41 'No AppArmor/SELinux confinement: Workloads declare no AppArmor or SELinux profile' implies a confinement gap on workloads that already run under seccomp RuntimeDefault and the restricted Pod Security Standard, where the container runtime applies its default AppArmor profile when none is declared.

D42 'No runtime threat detection: No runtime threat-detection engine (Tetragon TracingPolicy / Falco) is committed' expects cluster-level security infrastructure inside an application repository's manifests.

DM1 'Aggregate holds a reference to another aggregate' takes any entity with a private setter and a mutating method in a Domain namespace for an aggregate root, so a root holding its own child-entity collection is reported.
DM2 'Primitive id on a domain type: Appointment.PatientId is a raw Guid' applies a DDD strongly-typed-id expectation to a service whose ADRs record a layered, not DDD, design.

DM7 'Repository for a non-root entity: EquipmentRepository -> Equipment ... an entity but not an aggregate root' fires on repositories whose entity derives from AggregateRoot<TId>; the rows appeared only after the infrastructure project gained the EF design-time package and migrations.

ED3 'Event not named in past tense' and DM3 'Integration event couples to a producer-owned domain type' classify HTTP request/response records and contract summary DTOs (types under a *.Contracts namespace/folder) as events, although nothing publishes them.

ED5 'Possible non-idempotent mutation (review)' fires on a BackgroundService relay/dispatcher (a database save one hop away) whose idempotency is in the query predicate (only rows with DeliveredAt == null / not yet deleted) plus a message/event id consumers de-duplicate on — a guard the handler-body guard scan cannot see.

ED5 (both the structural 'Possible non-idempotent mutation (review)' row and the model-confirmed 'Non-idempotent mutation' row) treats an in-process Mediator command handler invoked from an HTTP POST as a message consumer subject to at-least-once redelivery.

ES3 'PII in event: ... Persisted event carries personal data (Email) — no crypto-shredding strategy' treats an integration event as a persisted (event-store) event because it is written to an outbox table, although the outbox row is deleted after publishing.

IC1 'Disabled test: ... coverage that looks present but never runs ... re-enable or delete it' fires on a skip whose reason is a categorised 'BUG:' naming a reproduced defect and its tracking issue URL.

M4 'README/code drift' publishes rows that come straight from the model's reading of the README ('reported by the model that read the README against this repository; no term search was run for this one, so nothing here has been checked against the tree') — an unverified claim is emitted as a finding.

M4 checks a README feature claim by matching model-chosen phrases ('CSV import functionality in CLI', 'typescript-eslint strict', 'React hooks rules') against file and directory NAMES and manifest text; when the phrase is not a name the implemented feature is reported as missing.

M4 drift rows assert a README claim the README does not make: a model-attributed project path the README never names, and a deterministic infra seed that reads the C4-model word 'containers' as 'Docker containerisation' — then 'confirm' the drift with a term search for the invented claim.

P2 'Logging is not universal: Only 5/7 service-like projects use logging' counts domain/adapter libraries — which the row itself says leave logging to their host — against universality, and misses the real gap (a worker using Console.WriteLine) because the project logs elsewhere.
P6 'Changelog looks stale/thin: carries N versioned entries, against a bar of 3' penalises a complete changelog of a project at its first release(s); the bar measures age, not changelog hygiene.
PF1 'No performance benchmarks' expects a BenchmarkDotNet suite in line-of-business/integration services with no performance-critical path.
PF2 'No allocation-aware APIs detected ... a bonus, not a requirement' is published as a finding for a service with no allocation-critical path.

PF3 'Awaits without ConfigureAwait(false): Only 4/50 awaits ... A library that captures the caller's context can stall or deadlock its host' counts awaits in ASP.NET Core / generic-host application projects, which have no SynchronizationContext.

R6 'The declared test suite includes a file that cannot be loaded: ... imports a module that names no file' treats a runtime directory URL built with `new URL('../../views/', import.meta.url)` as a module import.

R7 'Dead file: no import path from any entry point ... nothing in-repo names this module at all' fires on a compiled entry point that is run directly (`node dist/nightly.js`), named in the README but not in package.json scripts; the src->dist mapping of a run command is not an entry-point source.

R10 'Duplicated block (7 lines x 2 locations)' / 'with local edits' / 'concentrated across sibling directories' reports 5-10 line parallel accessors, shared call preludes (parse, look up, stop on a miss) and a 10-line HTML escaper duplicated across two separately compiled targets, where extraction would add indirection without removing a maintenance risk.
S1 'Weak hash algorithm: MD5/SHA1 is computed here' fires on MD5 used only to compute an HTTP ETag for cache validation.
X1 'Sync-over-async (deadlock risk): Blocking on a Task with .Wait()/.GetAwaiter().GetResult() can deadlock' fires in a console application's static Main.

X5 'Strict null checking is not enabled everywhere ... 0/2 configurations' reads compilerOptions of each tsconfig file without resolving `extends`, so strict inherited from a base config (here the @tsconfig/node22 package) is invisible.

X7 'Silent fallback default on parse failure: ExtractErrorCode falls back to "UNKNOWN" ... with no log or throw' judges the helper alone; the caller logs the sentinel with the HTTP status and throws it inside a CarrierException.

X14 'IP classification is bypassable through an IPv4-in-IPv6 embedding' keys on the absence of embedding-prefix tokens (6to4, NAT64, IPv4-compatible) and does not see that the IPv6 branch returns false (not public) for every IPv6 address that is not IPv4-mapped.

X15.name: Unvalidated length from an untrusted reader

X17.name: Uncapped recursion over a caller-supplied document

X24.name: Document value interpolated into markup unescaped

X28.name: Index access outside its own emptiness guard

X29.name: Per-element action decided by a fixed element

X30.name: Support guard that admits what it rejects

X31.name: Test-only surface in a production module

X32.name: Type resolved by simple name across every loaded assembly

errata.note: 1 of the 152 FNs (IAC-017) is a benchmark defect, not a scanner miss: line 34 of .github/workflows/pr-preview.yml is invalid YAML, so neither GitHub nor semgrep parses the file; with the line quoted, Watchdog's existing pull-request-target-code-checkout rule fires at line 16

falseNegativeMechanisms.title: No rule for the concept at all (scanner-neutral concepts beyond the reference scanner: unmapped or unevidenced in the mapping)
Repository-wide posture switches: one qualifying site anywhere credits the whole repository, so the defective site is never itemised (P7, P8, C2, S1, D40, D42, P10, P11, P6)

Code-health and test rules with no TypeScript arm (suppressions, commented-out code, empty catch, dead private code, @deprecated use, catch-rethrow, null dereference, swallowed test failures, mock dominance)

Pattern recognisers too shallow for the defect's shape (.Result, Assert.True(true), WarningsNotAsErrors, eslint config off-switches, Error('Not implemented'), hollow methods, density bars, bare floating promises, inert options, undrained stderr, vitest test without expect, truncation loops)

Prefix-less secrets: every vendor-prefixed secret was found, every secret without a vendor prefix was missed (punctuated Password=, credentials in connection URIs, inline Bearer, unquoted dotenv, .http files, Vite define)
Injection taint confined to the request handler: the tainted value arrives as a method parameter, model-bound argument, component state or ternary, or passes a function assumed safe (path.join)

Injection sink or library with no rule in the baked packs (Dapper, EF FromSqlRaw, Newtonsoft TypeNameHandling, ContentResult XSS, Redirect, Regex without timeout, MongoDB filters, dynamic RegExp, log injection, Blazor MarkupString)

Architecture / domain detectors read too narrow a population (project-reference cycles only, test edges in instability, no pass-through detection, attributes and projections ignored, entities without Id, declared references excuse co-change, test-support project not seen as test code)

Measured but never reported: per-site rows at Info/Recommendation level or below a score threshold never reach SARIF; only a location-less roll-up does (X2 CancellationToken, D12/npm outdated, R7 unused exports, R3 size)

Data-flow rules that match call NAMES, not data: source-generated [LoggerMessage] methods, structured log fields, headers inside a logged object, localStorage under a neutral key, MD5.HashData / createHash('md5') for passwords
DM9-DM11 have no TypeScript arm, and DM6/DM7 only partial ones (decorators only; no interface type arguments)
Found the file, missed the site: checkov/trivy Kubernetes rows at line 1 or the pod spec, a duplicate-block window that starts early, a misplaced dependency reported at its importer
Model-judged accessibility text cards (LA2 alt text, LA5 link text, LA6 labels) are composed only with a compliance framework configured, so the default configuration measures nothing
Dependency hygiene arms missing: npm deprecation not graded, EOL ignores engines.node and nested packages, R8 unused/undeclared blind on TypeScript
Presence-only runtime checks: X2 checks that a token parameter exists, not that it is forwarded; an injected fetch hides outbound HTTP from P7/X2; Console output is neither a log call nor flagged
ADR / documentation conformance is model-judged: absent from contained scans and unreliable in host passes (prose-enforced ADRs, README drift, ADR contradicted by an endpoint)
AC6 reads <style> blocks and inline styles only: motion and focus-outline defects in .css / .razor.css files are invisible
Flaky tests: detection is three re-runs (a 1e-4 flake never shows), no time-zone/clock-read rule, the fixed-sleep rule reads C# only
IaC / CI checks absent in the pinned rule sets: Ingress without TLS, pull_request_target checking out and building the PR head

C3 'Partial audit-trail evidence ... missing: an EF SaveChanges interceptor ... [Audited] per-entity coverage' asks for EF write-side hooks in a file-backed service that has no database and no entity write path.
C3 scores audit-trail evidence at 90 because an event-sourced stream exists, without checking that the stream covers the sensitive data or records the actor.
D1 'cyclomatic 17 (threshold 15)' fires on a method that is one flat disjunction of eight independent range tests with no nesting.

D10 'No assertions ... no assertion call was recognised' does not know CsCheck's Sample(predicate) (and similar property-based APIs), which throw CsCheckException with the shrunk counter-example when the predicate is false.
D14 matches banned SPDX ids as SUBSTRINGS of the resolved id (to catch -only/-or-later), so the banned 'GPL-2.0' matches 'LGPL-2.0-only' and an LGPL package is reported as GPL-banned.
D16 emits a repository-level 'Further sole-owners (lower concentration)' row for files below the off-boarding threshold without naming them, so the row cannot be acted on or adjudicated per file.

D17 'WriteOnlyPrivateField' reports a private System.Threading.Timer field that is assigned once and never read, although the field reference is what keeps the timer from being garbage-collected (and so keeps it firing).

D17 dead-code (SymbolFinder walk) reports an IDesignTimeDbContextFactory<T> implementation as unreferenced; dotnet-ef discovers and instantiates it by reflection, which the walk cannot see and no reflection-entry-point allow-list covers.
D20 model-judged ADR review flags 'The Consequences section is incomplete' when an ADR records its consequences but not the model's preferred list of benefits and trade-offs.
D21 model-judged naming reports two different concepts with a shared stem (a decision code `NoShow` and a fee amount `NoShowFee`) as one concept named inconsistently.

D26 'Projects may be oversized for their cohesion: 1 of 1 project(s) ... (repository root) 3011 LoC, 151 module-visible types across 18 directories' treats a single small TS service package as an oversized project to split.
The watchdog-authored D29 rule for DTD-enabled XmlDocument loading matches `SignedXml.LoadXml(XmlElement)` — a method on SignedXml that takes an already-parsed element and parses no text.

Semgrep 'unsafe-path-combine' reports Path.Combine(sourceDirectory, name) where the directory is the operator's own CLI argument (the trust boundary of an admin tool) and the name was validated against [A-Z0-9-]{1,32} before use.
Semgrep 'xpath-injection' (security-audit) reports an XPath built from a value that was passed through XmlConvert.VerifyNCName, which the rule does not model as a sanitiser.

watchdog-assembled-code-string-evaluated-ts reports `new Function` over source assembled only from a fixed table keyed by a schema-validated enum and a literal '1'/'-1' sign — no request text reaches the string.

watchdog-open-redirect-default-operand-js fires on `res.redirect(sameSitePath(req.query.returnTo) ?? '/')`: the left operand is a same-site-path validator's return value, but the rule treats any expression containing req.query as the raw request value.
D31 republishes checkov CKV_K8S_38 'Ensure that Service Account Tokens are only mounted where necessary' on a DaemonSet whose configuration queries the API server, i.e. where the token is necessary.

D41 'No AppArmor/SELinux confinement: Workloads declare no AppArmor or SELinux profile' implies a confinement gap on workloads that already run under seccomp RuntimeDefault and the restricted Pod Security Standard, where the container runtime applies its default AppArmor profile when none is declared.

D42 'No runtime threat detection: No runtime threat-detection engine (Tetragon TracingPolicy / Falco) is committed' expects cluster-level security infrastructure inside an application repository's manifests.
D8 emits 'Coverage not measured — no coverage collector is wired up' as a result row although it is an engine abstention ('excluded from score by design'), not a claim about the code.

IC1 'Disabled test: ... coverage that looks present but never runs ... re-enable or delete it' fires on a skip whose reason is a categorised 'BUG:' naming a reproduced defect and its tracking issue URL.
PF2 'No allocation-aware APIs detected ... a bonus, not a requirement' is published as a finding for a service with no allocation-critical path.

R6 'The declared test suite includes a file that cannot be loaded: ... imports a module that names no file' treats a runtime directory URL built with `new URL('../../views/', import.meta.url)` as a module import.

R7 'Dead file: no import path from any entry point ... nothing in-repo names this module at all' fires on a compiled entry point that is run directly (`node dist/nightly.js`), named in the README but not in package.json scripts; the src->dist mapping of a run command is not an entry-point source.
S1 'Weak hash algorithm: MD5/SHA1 is computed here' fires on MD5 used only to compute an HTTP ETag for cache validation.
X1 'Sync-over-async (deadlock risk): Blocking on a Task with .Wait()/.GetAwaiter().GetResult() can deadlock' fires in a console application's static Main.

X14 'IP classification is bypassable through an IPv4-in-IPv6 embedding' keys on the absence of embedding-prefix tokens (6to4, NAT64, IPv4-compatible) and does not see that the IPv6 branch returns false (not public) for every IPv6 address that is not IPv4-mapped.

X5 'Strict null checking is not enabled everywhere ... 0/2 configurations' reads compilerOptions of each tsconfig file without resolving `extends`, so strict inherited from a base config (here the @tsconfig/node22 package) is invisible.

X7 'Silent fallback default on parse failure: ExtractErrorCode falls back to "UNKNOWN" ... with no log or throw' judges the helper alone; the caller logs the sentinel with the HTTP status and throws it inside a CarrierException.
